brightness.note_plain: Horizons predicts V 16.9 to 17.9, brighter than our pipeline's 50% recovery limit, magnitude 17.7 (injection study aquarius-2025w23): it should stand out in these images. Horizons predicts visible-light brightness (V) while SPHEREx sees near-infrared light, so this is a rough comparison.

notes: 163 of 400 predicted positions are interpolated from Horizons' daily geocentric table (not computed from SPHEREx's own position), which can be off by several arcseconds for nearby objects.

response.summary_plain: JPL's predicted position of 2399 Terradas (1971 MA) falls inside 400 SPHEREx frames (the first ones are listed), in 69 visits from May 30, 2025 to Jan 2, 2026 (IRSA's public SPHEREx images run through Jan 10, 2026).
response.why_it_matters_plain: Old images that happen to show a known object are called precovery observations. Each one adds a position at a new date, which lengthens the stretch of time over which 2399 Terradas (1971 MA) has been observed. A longer observed arc pins down the orbit, so future positions can be predicted more precisely. The frames below are where SPHEREx's images should contain 2399 Terradas (1971 MA), according to JPL's current orbit.
